# Tariffs, Iran, and Rapid Impacts from AI

Report 183 | Published 2026-03-01 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-3-1/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/183.json)

Tariffs, war risk and AI economics.

The most consequential miss is the short Hormuz-disruption base case, contradicted by months of severe losses. The energy hedge rationale can still be useful despite that miss. Several AI business mechanisms are sensible conditional arguments, but adoption, causation and legal scope are less settled than the narrative sometimes suggests.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.
